intro: Apollo 12 landed in Oceanus Procellarum on November 19, 1969 — a pinpoint landing within walking distance of the Surveyor 3 robotic lander that had touched down 2½ years earlier. Conrad and Bean spent 31h on the surface across two EVAs, carried back 34 kg of samples plus pieces of Surveyor 3 for analysis. Demonstrated that crewed Apollo could reach a specific target on the lunar surface.

images.caption: Apollo 12 crew portrait — Pete Conrad (CDR), Dick Gordon (CMP), Al Bean (LMP).

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.subtitle: November 14, 1969 — struck by lightning twice in the first minute

images.caption: Saturn V SA-507 lifts off through a rain shower. Lightning hit the vehicle at T+36s and T+52s, knocking out fuel-cell power; SCE-to-AUX command saved the mission.
Conrad with the Surveyor 3 lander — Apollo 12 landed 163 m away, the first precision lunar landing.
ALSEP science station deployed — first long-duration lunar geophysical observatory.
